newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's March C/A deficit expands to $2.27 bln.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's March C/A deficit expands to $2.27 bln.

text.p: South Korea's current account shortfall widened to $2.27 billion in March from a $940.2 million deficit a year earlier, preliminary figures released by the central Bank of Korea (BOK) showed on Tuesday.
March Feb March 1996
Invisible trade -806.6 -593.5 -677.5
Note: figures are in millions of US dollars
The current account deficit for the first three months of this year jumped to $7.94 billion from a shortfall of $4.64 billion a year earlier.
The rising invisible trade deficit contributed to the widening current account deficit, a BOK statement said.
The statement said an improvement in cars and machinery exports helped reduce the March shortfall from a month ago.

Exports of vehicles and machinery rose year-on-year 11.0 percent and 15.2 percent respectively. But overseas shipments of heavy industrial goods slowed, falling 9.1 percent year-on-year in March from a 22.2 percent rise a year earlier.
A rise in imports of raw materials and consumer goods was also blamed for the widening trade deficit.

Imports of crude oil shot up by 155.3 percent to $1.76 billion in March from $690 million in the same period of last year. The statement said oil imports climbed on an oil price hike and an expansion of domestic refinery facilities.
But imports of capital goods fell by 1.6 percent in line with declining facility expansion by domestic companies as a result of a slowdown in the nation's economy.
The statement said imports of foreign-made electronic products, clothes and cosmetics continued to rise in March.
The rise in the invisible trade deficit was mainly due to an upsurge in interest payments, dividend payments and losses in futures trading by domestic financial institutions.
The travel deficit rose to $195.5 million in March from $137.7 million a year earlier.
Letters of credit received during March fell 10.8 percent to $6.15 billion against a 3.9 percent decline a year earlier.
The statement said South Korea posted a $2.73 billion capital surplus in March against $1.78 billion a year earlier.
The inflow of foreign funds rose as domestic companies issued large amounts of overseas equity-linked securities during the period, the statement said.
South Korea's overall balance of payments posted a $180 million surplus in March from a $850 million a year earlier.
Foreign currency reserves in the nation totalled $29.15 billion at the end of March from $29.76 billion a month ago.
